notes: phase cycles subtract the entry checkpoint cost (c1 - c0), which may overstate the in-phase checkpoint cost by a few cycles: phases may be a few cy short
load = a 4 B .nc load + the dependent address (LOP3, LEA, LEA.HI.X) + a dependent 16 B .nc load + the consuming shared store; every index and address is computed before entry

compute = the seed FADD + 256 dependent FFMA, fully unrolled (no loop control); compute_cycles_per_ffma per block count (warm launches; the first launch, the first fetch of this instantiation's code, in compute_cycles_per_ffma_cold) and per launch. It is compute / FFMA_N, so it carries a fixed per-warp term (the seed FADD and the checkpoint-cost residual, a few cycles: ~0.1 cy/FFMA at 64, ~0 at 4096) that falls with FFMA_N: compare across an --ffma sweep with a fit a + b * FFMA_N, not point by point. Hypotheses, not established: at 1 block/SM a rise of cycles/FFMA with FFMA_N (64..4096 = 1-64 KB of straight-line code) points at instruction-cache overflow; at 3 blocks/SM issue contention between overlapping warps also grows with FFMA_N; a cold sequential fetch cost per instruction is constant in FFMA_N and cannot be separated from the FFMA latency by the sweep (compare with the instr profile's isolated FFMA latency); Ampere/Hopper L0/L1 i-cache sizes are undocumented

barrier1/2 = the barrier + exactly the calibrated touch chain; tail = third barrier + shared load of (ticket, flag pointer) + writer predicate; flag_store = the predicated flag store alone (each checked on the measuring binary by its ktrace SASS check: these hold only if it says PASS)

scoreboard waits (SASS control bits): a timer or clock read inside a checkpoint may wait on an earlier instruction (usually a store's operand read). On a closing timer read it only widens that checkpoint's window; on an opening timer or clock read it delays the cycle value. NVRTC 12.9 builds: the bar1_release clock read (sm_80/86) waits on the pre-barrier calibration STS (already satisfied: the release LDS behind it has returned), the computed stamp's opening timer read on the barrier-1 touch STS (behind >= 64 dependent FFMA), the bar2_release and ticket closing timer reads (window only); the ktrace SASS check lists the waits of the binary that measured
ticket = warp 0 only (the atomic with return); the other 7 warps branch around it

flag write window = [max(flag checkpoint, flag value), exit checkpoint] of the writer warp (no value + tick bound); the writer is warp 0 of the block with ticket n_blocks - 1: a launch whose writer warp is missing (flag_writer_present false) or whose flag value is not that warp's flag-stamp timer read (flag_value_is_flag_stamp false) gets no window and no flag -> seen

exit excludes the writer's system fence (layout 1 included it: ~3.5k cy A100, ~1.8k cy RTX 3060): kernel_span_ns and last_exit_to_sync_return_ns are not comparable with layout 1; kernel_span_incl_writer_fence_ns and last_exit_incl_writer_fence_to_sync_return_ns are; writer_fence_cycles = writer's exit -> fence done (MEMBAR.SC.SYS + ERRBAR, as in layout 1, plus ~10 setup instructions incl. an S2R: a few tens of cycles), warm launches; the first launch's in writer_fence_cycles_cold
host-axis latencies carry the run's host<->GPU bound (bound_ns) in addition to the block bound
